newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Cultus ups oil estimates for Cornea field.
newsitem.headline: Cultus ups oil estimates for Cornea field.

text.p: Cultus Petroleum NL said on Thursday it had new estimates for its Cornea field offshore Western Australia which indicated between 617 million and 2,665 million barrels of oil were in place.
Company secretary Sam Russotti told Reuters the recovery rate was likely to be less than 50 percent.
Operator of the field's joint venture, Shell Oil's Shell Development (Australia) Pty Ltd, had previously indicated recoverable reserves of 200-400 million barrels.
Russotti said the latest figures were more detailed than previous data supplied by Shell.
Cultus had no production data and did not know what the recovery rate would be, he said.
"It will be under the half mark," he said. "We've got one sand which has very good permeability and the two other reservoir sands have got reasonable permeability."
"It's on a very large scale," Russotti said.
"It's a big field if these numbers turn out to be correct."

He said a typical Western Australian offshore oil field had about 200-400 million barrels of oil and joint venture partner Shell said in the past that the field could rival Australia's biggest, the Bass Strait field.
It was unlikely Cultus would have new information on the field's size before July when new exploration wells had been drilled.

After that, it could take anything up to three years before the field was in production. Cultus's share price was up 30 cents to NZ$4.20 in early afternoon trading and has rocketed from NZ$1.31 at the start of the year.
The reserves are based on the first three wells drilled in the field with the estimated hydrocarbon columns which range from 22-50 metres and pressure data.
Cultus said that the AC/P17 Joint Venture had secured the drill rig Sedco 703 and it would drill two exploration wells in the WA-241-P (Browse Basin) Joint Venture in the Cornea field.
The first of the wells will be Cornea South No.1 which is located on a southern lobe (possible extension) of the Cornea Structure and the estimated spud date is late June/early July.
The second well location will be determined upon results of the Cornea South No.1 well being known.

Shell Development have submitted to the WA-241-P/WA96-4 (WA-265-P)/WA96-5 (WA-266-P) Joint Ventures a forward exploration programme for the next 12 months consisting of a total of 13 wells and 2,100 sq km of 3D seismic acquisition.
Russotti said the Sedco 703 would drill further appraisal wells "because there are a lot of prospects within that permit(WA-241-P) and the other two permits that we haven't explored".
